claims.text: Machine-learning-accelerated high-throughput screening can predict optimal refractory high-entropy alloy compositions.
The predicted RHEA compositions can simultaneously exhibit intrinsic strength, ductility, and low weight.
Existing thermo-kinetic and simulation data can be leveraged to enable machine-learning prediction of desirable RHEA compositions.
High-throughput computational screening guided by machine learning can efficiently explore vast RHEA compositional spaces.
Controlled equilibrium processing and room-temperature testing reveal intrinsic material properties.
Phase stability and microstructural configuration govern the mechanical performance of RHEAs.
Formation of suitable solid-solution phases contributes to favorable mechanical performance.
Minimizing deleterious precipitates contributes to favorable mechanical performance.
A machine-learning model can identify complex composition-to-property correlations in RHEAs.
Selecting element combinations and concentrations that balance bonding, phase stability, and atomic-size effects can enhance alloy strength and ductility while reducing weight.
Machine-learning-guided screening will identify new RHEA compositions with significantly improved strength and ductility.
The identified RHEAs will have lower density than alloys produced through conventional design methods.
Traditional alloy-design simulations and iterative experimental validation are time-consuming.
The approach may not generalize to alloy systems with different training-data availability and underlying physical mechanisms.
The effectiveness of the machine-learning model depends on the availability and quality of RHEA data.
